main_body: Flat ground patch of dark olive-green grass, 4x3 tiles, repeating a tile pattern of lighter blade clumps, dark specks and a few gold and red flower pixels
top_band: none - terrain ground tile seen from above, no standing object
evidence: The kind is terrain: a flat ground texture with no standing volume, so the 3/4 top-plus-front contract does not apply. There is no object, no side face and no elevation drawing. It tiles cleanly as a ground fill. Nothing in the drawing fails the 3/4 contract for terrain.

style.evidence: The grass uses a dark olive base with about 4 green steps (base, darker clump, mid and light blade), plus sparse gold, red and brown accent pixels. The texture is a repetitive 16x16 tile pattern with vertical blade strokes and no large flat areas, so it is not flat. Compared with the Beodeul grass, which has clear clumps in several greens and a more varied layout, the candidate repeats an identical pattern every tile and is a little thinner in lightness range, with a muted, low-contrast ramp. The pixel-scattered look reads as noisy dithering more than shaped tufts. The flower dots are a decent touch. It sits a bit below the reference but is acceptable as a ground patch. Without an outline there is nothing to judge as sticker-like. Overall it is close to the reference in craft, with slightly lower tile density.
